probes.name: attack_no_placeholder_names
probes.description: NEGATIVE guard. The shipped defect was a fallback that rendered the literal string 'Mapped ATT&CK technique' as a technique description, so T1595 appeared in both PDFs with no name while looking like a resolved entry. This probe passes only while that string is ABSENT from production source; if it reappears the probe fails and the standard drops back to NOT_VERIFIED.

probes.name: wstg_is_a_testing_guide
probes.description: NEGATIVE-facing integrity check. WSTG is a TESTING guide: its entries are procedures against a running application. Without this disclaimer a report implying 'tested per WSTG' would be a false claim, because this tool performs static source analysis.

probes.name: wstg_static_attestability_declared

probes.name: wstg_licence_not_asserted

standards.title: CERT-In Technical Guidelines on SBOM, QBOM & CBOM, AIBOM and HBOM

probes.name: certin_vocabulary
probes.description: CERT-In minimum-element vocabulary is present in code.

probes.name: aibom_minimum_elements
probes.description: CERT-In Table 10 AIBOM minimum elements (intended and out-of-scope usage, preprocessing, training configuration, evaluation metrics) are captured.

probes.name: qbom_emitted
probes.description: A Quantum BOM is emitted (CERT-In Table 8, 11 minimum elements). The emitter is PARTIAL BY CONSTRUCTION: 6 of the 11 elements describe a physical quantum device that source analysis cannot observe. The artifact records each element's status and the reason, so partial coverage is visible rather than implied. QBOM here is the QUANTUM Bill of Materials per Chapter 8.1, not a Quality BOM.

probes.name: qbom_table8_elements
probes.description: CERT-In Table 8 QBOM minimum elements are enumerated by name, and each is marked OBSERVABLE or NOT_OBSERVABLE with a reason.

probes.name: qbom_never_invents_components
probes.description: NEGATIVE-facing integrity check. Quantum components are listed only when a resolved SBOM name matches a known quantum SDK, and whether detection found anything is stated explicitly. A QBOM that always contained an entry would be fabricated, since most codebases have no quantum dependency. The Attestations element is likewise marked as a content digest and not a digital signature.

probes.name: hbom_emitted
probes.description: A Hardware BOM is emitted (CERT-In Table 11, recursive). DELIBERATELY STILL FAILING. HBOM was deferred by the operator, and this probe is left failing rather than relaxed: a deferred item must keep the baseline honest, so CERT_IN cannot verify while it is outstanding. The Table 8 Hardware element is correspondingly null.

probes.name: csaf_emitted
probes.description: CSAF is supported; CERT-In section 6 requires VEX and CSAF for vulnerability state, and only VEX is present today.
